identity.title: REEF: Representation Encoding Fingerprints for Large Language Models

problem.claim: Determine whether a suspect LLM is a subsequent development of a victim model to help protect the victim model’s intellectual property.

contributions.claim: Proposes REEF, a training-free method that compares centered kernel alignment similarity between suspect- and victim-model representations on identical samples.
Reports that REEF preserves general capabilities and is robust to sequential fine-tuning, pruning, model merging, and permutations.

stated_novelty.claim: The proposed approach identifies model relationships from feature representations without training.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that REEF does not impair the model’s general capabilities.
The authors report robustness to sequential fine-tuning, pruning, model merging, and permutations.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM training requires substantial computation and data, making protection of open-source model intellectual property important.
Owners and third parties need to identify whether a suspect model derives from a victim model.
REEF addresses this by comparing centered kernel alignment between the two models’ representations on the same samples, without training.
The authors report capability preservation and robustness to several model transformations, positioning REEF as a simple protection mechanism.

source_observation.claim: The abstract defines the relationship test operationally through a specific representation similarity measure applied to the same samples.

lessons.interpretation: A concrete decision variable and controlled comparison make the proposed identification task easier to understand and evaluate.
lessons.application: When introducing a model-attribution method, explicitly state the compared objects, shared inputs, similarity metric, and whether training is required.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when attribution depends on outputs, metadata, or behavioral evidence rather than internal representations.

unknowns: The abstract provides no quantitative results, datasets, baselines, decision thresholds, or evaluation protocol.
It does not specify how similarity is converted into an identification decision or how robustness was measured.
The abstract states that code is publicly accessible but gives no reproducibility details beyond the repository link.
